This page is the way into the format. It shows what is on disk, why it is that
way, what review is asked for, and what has been tested. Most of it is folded:
open what you want to read.

Two reference documents sit behind it: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre-hub/blob/main/file-format/SPEC.md)
has the rules, numbered, and [`RATIONALE.md`](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre-hub/blob/main/file-format/RATIONALE.md)
has the full reasons, with evidence, under the same numbers.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Draft.** Nothing here has been reviewed. The format is version 0.1 until
sceptre's first release that uses it, which freezes it as 1.0.
:::

```{python}
#| include: false
import html
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import h5py
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

SCREEN = Path("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")
ANALYSIS = Path("example/highmoi/analyses/left_sided")
# every description on this page is read from the specification's own files
screen_spec = json.loads(Path("spec/screen.json").read_text())
table_spec = json.loads(Path("spec/tables.json").read_text())
ROWS = 5
pd.set_option("display.width", 120)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 12)


def text(value) -> str:
    """Plain text as HTML, with `code` spans."""
    return re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", r"<code>\1</code>", html.escape(str(value)))


def n(count, noun) -> str:
    return f"{count:,} {noun}{'' if count == 1 else 's'}"


def cell(value) -> str:
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return f"{value:.4g}"
    if hasattr(value, "__len__") and not isinstance(value, str):
        shown = ", ".join(f"{v:.3g}" for v in list(value)[:4])
        return f"[{shown}{', …' if len(value) > 4 else ''}]"
    return str(value)


def rows(frame: pd.DataFrame, index_name=None) -> str:
    """The first rows of a table."""
    head = frame.head(ROWS)
    if index_name is not None:
        head = head.rename_axis(index_name).reset_index()
    body = head.map(cell).to_html(index=False, border=0, classes="rows", escape=True)
    more = f"<p class='more'>… {n(len(frame) - len(head), 'more row')}</p>" if len(frame) > len(head) else ""
    return body + more


def columns(described: dict, present) -> str:
    """What the specification says about the columns that are present."""
    items = [f"<li><code>{html.escape(c)}</code>: {text(described[c])}</li>" for c in present if c in described]
    return f"<ul class='columns'>{''.join(items)}</ul>" if items else ""


def as_json(value) -> str:
    return f"<pre>{html.escape(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))}</pre>"


def row(name, what, size, depth, folder=False) -> str:
    tag = "summary"
    folder = " folder" if folder else ""
    return (f"<{tag} class='row{folder}' style='--d:{depth}'><span class='name'><code>{html.escape(name)}</code></span>"
            f"<span class='what'>{text(what)}</span><span class='size'>{html.escape(size)}</span></{tag}>")


def leaf(name, what, size, body, depth) -> str:
    return f"<li><details>{row(name, what, size, depth)}<div class='body'>{body}</div></details></li>"


def branch(name, what, size, children, depth) -> str:
    """A folder or a group: closed at first, except the top one."""
    return f"<li><details{' open' if depth == 0 else ''}>{row(name, what, size, depth, True)}<ul>{''.join(children)}</ul></details></li>"


def kilobytes(path) -> str:
    files = [path] if path.is_file() else [f for f in path.rglob("*") if f.is_file()]
    return f"{sum(f.stat().st_size for f in files) / 1024:,.0f} KB"


def as_tree(top) -> str:
    return ("<div class='tree'><div class='bar'><button onclick=\"treeAll(this, true)\">Open all folders</button>"
            f"<button onclick=\"treeAll(this, false)\">Close all</button></div><ul>{top}</ul></div>")


def screen_tree() -> str:
    says = screen_spec["descriptions"]
    in_every_modality = {c["name"]: c["description"] for c in screen_spec["cell_tables"]["every_modality"]}
    in_grna_table = {c["name"]: c["description"] for c in screen_spec["grna_table"]}
    children = []
    with h5py.File(SCREEN) as f:
        for name in sorted(f["mod"], key=lambda m: m == screen_spec["modalities"]["grna"]):
            grna = name == screen_spec["modalities"]["grna"]
            counts = ad.io.read_elem(f[f"mod/{name}/X"])
            obs, var = ad.io.read_elem(f[f"mod/{name}/obs"]), ad.io.read_elem(f[f"mod/{name}/var"])
            corner = pd.DataFrame(counts[:ROWS, :6].toarray(), index=obs.index[:ROWS], columns=var.index[:6])
            shape = f"{n(counts.shape[0], 'cell')} × {n(counts.shape[1], 'gRNA' if grna else 'feature')}"
            children.append(branch(f"mod/{name}", says["grna_modality" if grna else "modality"], shape, [
                leaf("X", says["counts"], n(counts.nnz, "nonzero count"),
                     "<p class='more'>The first cells and features:</p>" + rows(corner, "cell") + "<p class='more'>…</p>", 2),
                leaf("obs", says["cell_table"], f"{n(len(obs), 'row')} × {n(obs.shape[1], 'column')}",
                     columns(in_every_modality, obs.columns) + rows(obs, "cell"), 2),
                leaf("var", says["grna_table" if grna else "feature_table"], f"{n(len(var), 'row')} × {n(var.shape[1], 'column')}",
                     (columns(in_grna_table, var.columns) if grna else "") + rows(var, "gRNA" if grna else "feature"), 2),
            ], 1))
        shared = ad.io.read_elem(f["obs"])
        children.append(leaf("obs", says["shared_cell_table"], f"{n(len(shared), 'row')} × {n(shared.shape[1], 'column')}", rows(shared, "cell"), 1))
        stamp = ad.io.read_elem(f[screen_spec["metadata"]["path"]])
        entries = screen_spec["metadata"]["entries"]
        values = pd.DataFrame([{"entry": k, "value": str(v), "meaning": entries.get(k, {}).get("description", "")} for k, v in stamp.items()])
        values["meaning"] = values["meaning"].str.replace("`", "")
        children.append(leaf(screen_spec["metadata"]["path"], says["metadata"], f"{len(values)} entries", values.to_html(index=False, border=0, classes="rows", escape=True), 1))
    return as_tree(branch(SCREEN.name, says["file"], kilobytes(SCREEN), children, 0))


def table_leaf(path, what, depth) -> str:
    file = pq.ParquetFile(path)
    frame = file.read().to_pandas()
    body = rows(frame)
    identity = (file.metadata.metadata or {}).get(table_spec["fits"]["identity_key"].encode())
    if identity is not None:
        body = "<p class='more'>How these fits were made, stored inside the file:</p>" + as_json(json.loads(identity)) + body
    return leaf(path.name, what, f"{n(len(frame), 'row')} × {n(frame.shape[1], 'column')}", body, depth)


def analysis_tree() -> str:
    says = table_spec["descriptions"]
    of_table = {t["name"]: t["description"] for t in table_spec["tables"]}
    children = [leaf("analysis.json", says["analysis.json"], "", as_json(json.loads((ANALYSIS / "analysis.json").read_text())), 1)]
    for stage in table_spec["stages"]:
        folder = ANALYSIS / stage
        if not folder.is_dir():
            continue
        inside = [table_leaf(folder / f"{name.split('/')[1]}.parquet", what, 2)
                  for name, what in of_table.items() if name.startswith(f"{stage}/") and (folder / f"{name.split('/')[1]}.parquet").exists()]
        inside.append(leaf("record.json", says["record.json"], "", as_json(json.loads((folder / "record.json").read_text())), 2))
        children.append(branch(f"{stage}/", says["stages"][stage], n(len(inside), "file"), inside, 1))
    fits = ANALYSIS / table_spec["fits"]["folder"]
    if fits.is_dir():
        parts = [table_leaf(p, says["part"], 2) for p in sorted(fits.glob("*.parquet"))]
        children.append(branch(f"{table_spec['fits']['folder']}/", says["fits"], n(len(parts), "file"), parts, 1))
    return as_tree(branch(f"{ANALYSIS.name}/", says["analysis"], kilobytes(ANALYSIS), children, 0))


# What each check of the verification suite shows, and what it found when this page was rendered.
SHOWS = {
    "conformance": "Both validators report exactly the expected rules on every file of `conformance/` (files that conform, and files that each break a rule), and the standard readers read the files that must still be read",
    "encodings": "Every kind of value, written by each language's standard libraries and read by the other's. The kinds the format allows come back correct; the kinds it forbids still break",
    "two-writers": "R and Python each write the same random content. The files are compared array by array and column by column, and each language reads the other's file and gets the source back",
    "independent-readers": "Tools outside this code read the files: anndata, scanpy, pandas, polars and duckdb in Python; HDF5Array and arrow in R",
    "wide-index": "The 64-bit branch of the count matrix's index type, with the limit lowered because no test file reaches it",
    "writers": "What a writer does beyond producing a conforming file: a copy keeps the dataset's identifier and every modality, a retried stage leaves nothing of its first attempt, and large matrices get 64-bit index arrays",
    "derived": "What software computes from the files (cells per gRNA and per target, cells in use, pairs passing QC, log2 fold change, significance, control groups) equals what sceptre itself computed",
}


def status() -> str:
    found = {}
    for path in sorted(Path("verify/out/results").glob("*.json")):
        name, language = path.stem.rsplit("-", 1)
        found.setdefault(name, {})[language] = [c["result"] for c in json.loads(path.read_text())]
    cases = {c["name"]: c for c in json.loads(Path("conformance/cases.json").read_text())}
    for language in ("r", "python"):
        results = json.loads(Path(f"conformance/results-{language}.json").read_text())
        found.setdefault("conformance", {})[language] = [
            "pass" if name not in cases or (sorted(r["rules"]) == cases[name]["expect"] and r["conforms"] == cases[name]["conforms"]
                                            and False not in [v for k, v in r.items() if k != "conforms"]) else "fail"
            for name, r in results.items()]
    if set(found) != set(SHOWS) or any(set(v) != {"r", "python"} for v in found.values()):
        raise SystemExit("Run verify/run.sh before rendering: this page reports its results.")

    def passed(results) -> str:
        fails = results.count("fail")
        return f"{results.count('pass'):,} of {len(results):,}" + ("" if fails == 0 else " — FAILING")
    lines = "".join(f"<tr><td><code>{name}</code></td><td>{text(SHOWS[name])}</td><td>{passed(found[name]['r'])}</td><td>{passed(found[name]['python'])}</td></tr>" for name in SHOWS)
    return f"<table class='status'><thead><tr><th>Check</th><th>What it shows</th><th>Passed in R</th><th>Passed in Python</th></tr></thead><tbody>{lines}</tbody></table>"
```

<script>
function treeAll(button, open) {
  const tree = button.closest(".tree");
  // folders only: a file's contents open on a click of its own
  tree.querySelectorAll("details").forEach(d => { if (d.querySelector(":scope > ul")) d.open = open; else if (!open) d.open = false; });
  if (!open) tree.querySelector("details").open = true;
}

## The principles

Every choice in the format follows from these eight. Where two of them pull
apart, the earlier one wins. Open one for its reason and what follows from it.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# read from the table of section 2 of RATIONALE.md, so the two cannot differ
lines = Path("RATIONALE.md").read_text().split("## 2. The eight principles")[1].split("\n---")[0].splitlines()
for line in lines:
    cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split(" | ")]
    if len(cells) == 4 and cells[0].isdigit():
        number, principle, why, follows = cells
        follows = follows.replace("](#", "](https://github.com/Katsevich-Lab/sceptre-hub/blob/main/file-format/RATIONALE.md#")
        print(f'<details class="fold">\n<summary><strong>{number}. {html.escape(principle.strip("*"))}</strong></summary>\n')
        print(f"- **Why.** {why}\n- **What follows.** {follows}\n\n</details>\n")
```

## What is on disk

A screen is **one file**. An analysis of it is **one folder**, kept apart from
the data, and one screen can have any number of analyses. Both trees below are
read from the example in `example/highmoi/`. Open a folder to see its files,
and a file to see what it holds.

### The data file

A standard MuData `.h5mu` file, written once and never modified. It holds raw
counts and what is known about the cells and the gRNAs, and nothing an
analysis computes.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(screen_tree())
```

### An analysis

One subfolder per completed stage. Tables are Parquet files, and every row
names cells, gRNAs and responses by identifier, never by position.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(analysis_tree())
```

## Open these files yourself

Standard libraries read both, in R or Python. Nothing here is specific to sceptre.

screen <- MuData::readH5MU("example/highmoi/screen.h5mu")
screen

## The choices to review

These are the choices that cannot change after the format is frozen without
breaking existing files. Disagreement is cheap now and costly then. Each opens
to its reason and the alternative it was chosen over; the label after each
is the section of `RATIONALE.md` (and of `SPEC.md`) with the detail.

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Data and analysis are separate.</strong> <span class="where">S12</span></summary>

- **The choice.** The data file holds nothing an analysis produces: no assignments, no kept-or-removed flag, no results. Each analysis is its own folder.
- **Why.** One dataset has many analyses, and the data file is then written once and never touched again. Keeping a kept-or-removed flag in the data file, as public pysceptre does, means rewriting the whole file to work on the kept cells.
- **Instead of.** One self-contained file holding data, assignments and results, which is the IGVF pipeline's layout and suits uploading one file to a portal.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>The data is one MuData <code>.h5mu</code> file.</strong> <span class="where">S1</span></summary>

- **Why.** MuData is the scverse standard for one set of cells measured in several ways. Standard libraries open it in both languages, and one file is easy to move and publish.
- **Instead of.** A Zarr store, two `.h5ad` files, the `ondisc` format, or a folder of Parquet and matrix files.
- **Locks in.** HDF5. A Zarr variant could be added later without changing anything else.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Counts are stored by feature.</strong> <span class="where">S3</span></summary>

- **The choice.** The count matrix is cells × features, column-compressed, so one gene is one contiguous read.
- **Why.** Every stage works gene by gene. With counts stored by cell, the IGVF pipeline first splits the whole file into per-gene chunk files.
- **Cost.** A file from another tool is usually stored by cell and is converted once at import.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Modalities are named for what was measured, and the analysis says which one it tests.</strong> <span class="where">S2, A1</span></summary>

- **The choice.** The gRNA modality is always `grna`. Every other modality is named for its measurement (`rna`, `protein`, ...). `analysis.json` names the response modality; nothing finds it by a fixed name.
- **Why.** A file can then hold a second measured modality, and any modality can become the response of a later analysis.
- **Instead of.** A fixed role name such as `response`, which is what both packages use in memory today.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Covariate names carry the modality's name: <code>rna_n_umis</code>, not <code>response_n_umis</code>.</strong> <span class="where">S5</span></summary>

- **The choice.** Facts about the cell (batch, donor) are in the shared cell table. Measurements of a modality are in that modality's cell table. A model's covariate table prefixes each modality's columns with its name.
- **Why.** A batch belongs to the cell, not to its RNA. A role prefix cannot name the RNA depth in an analysis whose response is protein.
- **Cost.** Formulas users write today say `response_n_umis`. The packages can keep accepting that name and translate.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>One folder per stage, with a record written last.</strong> <span class="where">A2</span></summary>

- **The choice.** Each completed stage has a folder holding its tables and `record.json`: the stage's settings, provenance and list of files. The record is written after the tables.
- **Why.** No file is ever rewritten. The record marks the stage as finished, so a folder without one is a stage that did not finish. Calibration, power and discovery do not depend on one another and could run at once without racing for one file. Rerunning a stage is deleting its folder.
- **Instead of.** One settings file rewritten by every stage, or tables grouped by kind with stage ownership recorded elsewhere.
- **The stage names** are `parameters`, `assignment`, `qc`, `calibration`, `power`, `discovery`.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Tables name things by identifier and are sorted by key.</strong> <span class="where">T0, T5</span></summary>

- **Why.** Tables then survive subsetting, reordering and being written in pieces by parallel jobs, and there is no question of counting from 0 or from 1.
- **Consequence.** Results are sorted by target and response, not by p-value.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Assignments are a table of (gRNA, cell) rows, not a matrix.</strong> <span class="where">T1</span></summary>

- **Why.** The assignment belongs to an analysis, not to the data. The table is tiny next to the counts, parallel jobs can each write a part, and another tool can hand in a plain two-column table. A table of 10 million rows reads in about 8 seconds in Python and 10 in R.
- **Instead of.** A 0/1 cells × gRNAs matrix in the data file, which is what the IGVF pipeline, pertpy and public pysceptre use. The two hold the same information.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Saved model fits are a cache outside the stages.</strong> <span class="where">T6</span></summary>

- **The choice.** `fits/response/` holds part files. Each part says, inside the file, how its fits were made, and software uses a part only when that matches what it would do itself. Deleting the folder changes no result.
- **Why.** A fit depends on the data, the formula, the fitting method, the control group and the cells that passed QC, all fixed once QC has run. Which testing stage computes it first is an accident, so a stage's folder is the wrong home: rerunning that stage would delete fits that are still valid.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>The design matrix is not stored, and formulas are additive only.</strong> <span class="where">T7</span></summary>

- **The choice.** The parameters record holds the formula text and the names of the matrix's columns. Each language rebuilds the matrix and checks those names.
- **Evidence.** On the example, R and pysceptre build matrices that are equal to the last bit on one machine.
- **Cost.** Only additive formulas of covariates, `log(x)` and `log(x + 1)` can be saved. An analysis with an interaction or a spline cannot.
- **No hash of the matrix.** A hash of exact values would fail on a correct matrix, because a logarithm's last bit differs between macOS and Linux (measured). A check that survives this can be added later.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>Nothing is stored that follows from something else stored.</strong> <span class="where">S6, T5</span></summary>

- **Examples.** Results have no `significant` column, and `log_2_fold_change` is stored only where there is no `fold_change` to derive it from.
- **The exception.** Each cell's total count and number of nonzero features are stored, because recomputing them is a full pass over the counts and nearly every analysis needs them.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>A two-part version in every file.</strong> <span class="where">S10</span></summary>

- **The choice.** The data file and each analysis carry their own `MAJOR.MINOR`. A minor increase adds something older software can ignore. A major increase is any change after which older software could misread a file, and software refuses a major version it does not know.

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary><strong>The names.</strong> <span class="where">SPEC, sections 2 to 4</span></summary>

Column, table and file names are as hard to change as structure: `grna_target`, `target_chr`, `target_start`, `target_end`, `vector_id`, `n_umis`, `n_nonzero`, `pass_qc`, `p_value`, `fold_change`, and the table names in the tree above. If one reads wrongly to you, now is the time to say so.

</details>

## Questions for reviewers

1. **Is the scope right?** The format fixes the form of results and leaves their meaning (what a p-value tests) to sceptre's method documentation.
2. **Is anything missing that a real screen needs?** For gRNA annotation the format has a target, its position and an optional vector, and no gRNA type or spacer sequence yet.
3. **Coordinates.** Target positions are 1-based with both ends included, as in GTF files, and a file with positions has to say which genome build they are in. Is that the right convention?
4. **Limits.** A gRNA has one target, and so does a vector carrying several gRNAs; combinatorial screens are refused. DNA-targeting is assumed. Are those limits acceptable for now?
5. **The fitting-method default.** Saved fits are shared between R and Python only when the method matches, and the current default differs from the alternatives on a few responses. This is a scientific decision the format does not make.
6. **Additive formulas only.** Is it acceptable that an analysis with an interaction or a spline cannot be saved?

<details class="fold">
<summary>What does not need review now</summary>

These can be added or changed later without breaking any file.

- **Optional columns and tables not yet in the format:** gRNA type, spacer, gene annotation, per-cell QC reasons, assignment scores (`RATIONALE.md`, section 9).
- **The wording of individual rules.** The sorting into file rules, behaviour rules and guidance is meant to be final; the sentences are not.
- **Compression settings and Parquet details.** Software reading the files does not depend on them.
- **The code in `format/`.** It is a prototype that shows the format works in both languages, and is replaced by code in sceptre and pysceptre.
- **The comparisons with IGVF and pertpy** (`RATIONALE.md`, section 8), unless you know those formats and see an error.

</details>

## What has been tested

`verify/run.sh` runs every check, using neither sceptre nor pysceptre. The
counts below are from the run this page was rendered after.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(status())
```

- **Once, at scale:** the data file, on a real screen of 207,324 cells, written by both languages to identical files and read back in memory and from disk.
- **Once, with both packages:** each example analysis was rebuilt as a sceptre object and as a pysceptre analysis from the files. Nothing here repeats that; it returns when the packages adopt the format.

**Not tested.**

- A real analysis larger than 1,000 cells. Its tables were measured at real size with made-up content; `scale-test/README.md` has the numbers and what they suggest changing.
- Windows. The suite passes on macOS and on Linux.
- Real data in a second measured modality.
- Count matrices past the 32-bit index limit. The 64-bit types are handled; values that large are not exercised.
- An implementation by someone else. One author wrote the specification and both prototypes.

`SPEC.md` marks each rule with how it is checked, including the rules nothing tests.

## What is in the repository

<details class="fold">
<summary>The folders and files of <code>file-format/</code></summary>

| Folder or file | What it is |
|---|---|
| `notebook.qmd`, `notebook.html` | This page and its source. `./render.sh` renders it |
| `SPEC.md` | The specification: scope, terms, and numbered statements sorted into file rules, behaviour rules and guidance |
| `RATIONALE.md` | The reasons: every choice with its alternatives and evidence, comparisons with the IGVF pipeline's format and with pertpy, planned additions, and the measurements |
| `spec/` | The machine-readable parts: `screen.json` (the structure of a data file), `tables.json` (every table's columns, types and key) and JSON Schemas for the JSON records. The descriptions in the trees above are read from here |
| `format/` | The prototype: writers and validators in R and Python, with the same names. It uses neither sceptre nor pysceptre |
| `example/` | Files in the format: a high-MOI dataset with six analyses, a low-MOI dataset with one, and a small synthetic data file with every kind of column. `example/*/expected/` holds values sceptre itself computed for each analysis |
| `conformance/` | Files that conform and files that each break a rule, with what a validator must report |
| `verify/` | The verification suite, and how to test another implementation against the same files |
| `scale-test/` | Recorded results of the run on 207,324 cells |

</details>

<details class="fold">
<summary>How the format is defined, and where the code will live</summary>

- **The format is `SPEC.md` and `spec/`.** The validators, `validate_screen()` and `validate_analysis()`, exist in R and in Python and decide whether a file conforms. There is no canonical writer.
- **A data file is read with standard libraries:** `mudata.read_h5mu` in Python, `MuData::readH5MU` in R. The format has no reader of its own.
- **Writers are custom.** Each is a wrapper around the standard writer that stays inside what both languages read correctly. The two here are temporary: they move into sceptre and pysceptre, which become the reference implementations.

</details>
